title: Give each test run its own log file instead of one shared path
tier_reason: a habit of mine, written down so the next session does not repeat it
ask:
Through the 2026-09-07 session every integration run was redirected to the same scratchpad path and then grepped for its result. When an earlier run outlived its shell — see the companion item about the suite not exiting — a live writer and a reader shared one file, and a result could have been read that belonged to another run. It did not go wrong that day (a clean re-run matched), but it is a way to believe a number that is not yours.

The habit to keep: one log path per run, named for the run, and check the file's size or the process's exit code before believing a grep. A grep that finds nothing means 'never started' at least as often as it means 'still running' — that mistake cost several rounds of the same session, reporting a suite as running when it had died on a parse error in one second.
first_action: No code to change — this is guidance for whoever runs the suites next.
why: Reported results are the whole basis on which work gets committed and deployed.
model_note: Opus for now: the week's Fable budget is spent (Daniel, 2026-09-21). Remove this field to return to the seat's default.
result: Closed as an operator habit already supported by the current runners. tools/run_godot_test.py starts each Godot invocation with a private XDG_DATA_HOME, reads that child’s own output, requires a Results line, and returns a nonzero status for a missing result, script error, failed count, timeout, or nonzero child exit. hq/run_tests.py captures each test file’s output and exit status in its own subprocess and per-file scratch directory. CI invokes the Godot wrapper separately for Unit tests, Integration tests, Robot session, and Sim benchmark. For any manual redirection, give each invocation a new log path named for that run; check its process exit code or that its log is nonempty before interpreting a grep. An empty grep is not evidence that the suite is still running. This is separate from the companion suite-exit issue. Focused local checks: hq/tests/test_hq_test_runner.py passed 3/3; tools/test_process_integrity.py passed 6/6 after the CI-style Godot import. An initial unimported run failed 1/6 with missing script/audio imports and exited 1; its distinct nonempty log made that failure visible. No runner code change was needed.
